question: A circular coil having ‘n’ turns produces a field ______________ times large as that produced by a single turn
solution:
The correct answer is __**n**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A circular coil having **'n'** turns produces a field **n** times larger than that produced by a single turn.
 
• This is because the magnetic field produced by each turn of the coil adds up linearly when the turns are in series.
 
• Therefore, if a single turn produces a magnetic field of strength **B**, then **n** turns will produce a magnetic field of strength **nB**.
 
• This relationship is crucial in applications where stronger magnetic fields are required, such as in electromagnets and inductors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The strength of the magnetic field in a coil is also influenced by factors such as the current flowing through the coil and the core material used.
 
• Using a ferromagnetic core can significantly increase the magnetic field strength compared to an air core.
 
• The formula for the magnetic field strength at the center of a circular coil is given by **B = (μ₀ * n * I) / (2 * R)**, where **μ₀** is the permeability of free space, **n** is the number of turns, **I** is the current, and **R** is the radius of the coil.
